source.title: AttentionInfluence: Adopting Attention Head Influence for Weak-to-Strong Pretraining Data Selection
source.authors: Kai Hua; Steven Z. Wu; Ge Zhang; Ke Shen

page_placements.theme: Retrieval heads in long-context retrieval, many-shot ICL and grounded generation

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses retrieval-head masking to select pretraining data, but does not identify or test induction heads as defined in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports an in-context-learning evaluation after masking retrieval heads and describes retrieval-head evolution during training. These heads are not shown to be induction heads. Results on downstream benchmarks and data selection are not rows because they do not measure the claimed induction-head behavior.
record.test_reason: The study uses retrieval-head masking (heads chosen by a copy-paste score on a synthetic key-value task) as a tool for pretraining data selection. It never identifies induction heads, previous-token composition, a phase change, or loss against token index. Its ICL ablation and retrieval-head evolution concern a related but different construct, so they go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that masking retrieval heads in a small model gives a training-free loss-gap signal for selecting reasoning-intensive pretraining data, improving a 7B model on benchmarks such as MMLU, GSM8K and HumanEval. They also note retrieval heads matter for ICL and reasoning. They make no claim about induction heads per se.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a synthetic key-value retrieval task to rank retrieval heads, masks the top 5% by equalizing their attention weights, and uses loss differences for data selection; it does not reproduce the induction-head mechanism or phase-change measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports retrieval-head evolution across training checkpoints and compares retrieval-head masking with random non-retrieval-head masking.

fits_no_version.finding: Masking top-5% retrieval heads in a 1.3B model drops Banking77-en-ICL from 0.4148 to 0.0001. Randomly masking other heads gives 0.3840.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a 1.3B LLaMA2-like model, heads selected by a synthetic key-value copy task are necessary for many-shot ICL classification.

fits_no_version.finding: Retrieval heads emerge early, gradually strengthen, and become entrenched by mid-to-late training (Figure 2, checkpoints 5B–1499B tokens).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Retrieval-head strength in a 1.3B model grows gradually across pretraining checkpoints.

record.problems: The paper studies retrieval heads rather than identifying induction heads. The reported in-context-learning ablation is for one 1.3B model and one internal evaluation task; no uncertainty estimates are stated. Retrieval-head evolution values are shown only in a figure, with the trend summarized in text.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream benchmark and data-selection results were omitted because they do not measure induction-head behavior or its predicted formation.

untested.parts: Abrupt formation, its timing against ICL gains, and the loss bump.
Induction heads' share of in-context learning in large models.
Induction heads across families, sizes, architectures and modalities.
Effect of data or training setup on induction-head formation or ICL persistence.
Whether few-shot learning runs through non-induction heads.
Whether formation is one transition or several sub-steps.

record.verdict_notes: The paper cites Olsson et al. only as motivation. The retrieval score (copy of the max-attended token) is related to induction or copying behaviour, but no induction-head identification is made. The masking also replaces attention with uniform weights rather than mean-ablating the heads.

versions.untested_parts: Whether induction heads compose with previous-token heads or implement the [A][B] … [A] → [B] pattern.
Induction-head formation, its timing relative to in-context-learning gains, and a training-loss bump.
Whether induction heads explain most in-context learning in large transformers; the study tests retrieval-head masking in a 1.3B model but does not establish those heads are induction heads.
Induction behavior across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.
How data or training setup affects induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning.
Whether few-shot learning is mainly carried by mechanisms other than induction heads.
Whether induction-head formation comprises separate or overlapping transitions.

The state should be cannot_determine, not observed, relative to the versions.

relation.reason: Uses the head-based mechanistic finding to construct a weaker reference model, without identifying induction heads or testing their mechanism, phase change, or contribution to loss falling with token index.

tranche.reason: Uses attention-head importance for in-context learning and reasoning to motivate retrieval-head masking as a data-selection tool; does not test any induction-head claim version.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased. Retrieval heads are not established to be induction heads; Banking77-en-ICL measures many-shot classification, and the six training checkpoints do not resolve an early induction-head transition.
